urn:eigenius:core:description: Binding kinetics for a kinase inhibitor: `compound + kinase ⇌ complex`. Forward rate `k_on` (1/(nM·s)), reverse rate `k_off` (1/s). Dissociation constant Kd = k_off / k_on relates to the assay-level IC50 via Cheng-Prusoff. Three species, two reactions (one reversible split into forward + backward), two parameters.
urn:eigenius:julia:catalyst:network_sour:
@reaction_network begin
    k_on,  C + K --> CK
    k_off, CK --> C + K
end

urn:eigenius:core:description: Total compound (free + bound) is conserved: `C + CK = constant`. Coefficients [1, 0, 1] aligned with species [C, K, CK]. AutoOnLoad confirms via `Catalyst.conservationlaws`.
Total kinase (free + bound) is conserved: `K + CK = constant`. Coefficients [0, 1, 1].

The compound-kinase-binding network has structural deficiency = 0 — Feinberg formula: 2 complexes (C+K, CK) − 1 linkage class − 1 stoichiometric rank = 0. By Feinberg's deficiency-zero theorem, this guarantees a unique positive steady state in each compatibility class for any positive rate constants.
Both reactions are present in opposite directions, so the network is weakly reversible.

Steady-state concentrations for the compound-kinase-binding network parameterised at Kd = 42 nM (matching EIG_0042 vs CDK2 from R0001). Initial conditions Ctot = Ktot = 100 nM. Solution: CK ≈ 52.87 nM, C = K ≈ 47.13 nM. AutoOnLoad re-solves and confirms within tolerance.
